results.title: The Theory of Monads and the Monad Laws | Good Math/Bad Math
results.snippet: But example, for example, a law like this: f >>= return = f Expanding bind: join (fmap return f) = f This is true for all f, so: join . fmap return = id Which you will recognise as one of the category theory properties above.

results.title: Monad (functional programming)
results.snippet: Although Haskell defines monads in terms of the return and bind functions, it is also possible to define a monad in terms of return and two other operations, join and fmap. This formulation fits more closely with the definition of monads in category theory.
